subject: DPA: proposed handback window and tiered TTL carve-outs
messages:
From: Tom Bennett <tom.bennett@astrahealth.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
Cc: legal@astrahealth.com
Date: 2028-06-10T09:12:00Z
Subject: DPA redline — handback window and TTL carve-outs

Hi Hannah,

Thanks for sending the revised DPA. Our legal team reviewed the retention/deletion sections and flagged two areas we need clearer contractual commitments on before we can proceed:

1) Handback/Return window on termination — section 6.2 in our redline asks for a 30-day handback period during which we can request a final snapshot and transfer of onshore copies.

2) Tiered TTL carve-outs — we proposed language carving logs, ephemeral inference cache, and backups into separate categories with different maximum retention periods (e.g., logs 180 days, backups 90 days, ephemeral cache 30 days). We also requested that backups containing EU resident derived data be kept only onshore unless explicit consent is provided.

Two follow-up asks from our side:
- Certificate of erasure: we need a signed attestation within 21 days after deletion for primary copies and a 90-day attestation window for backups.
- Snapshot replication: if snapshots are replicated for DR, we need the contract to limit cross-border replication for EU-resident data to within EU-operated regions (AstraHealth will accept narrow exceptions for transient diagnostic copies).

I've attached our redline PDF — highlights added. Can your team propose concrete compromise language for the handback window and TTL carve-outs?

Appreciate a quick read — we are on a product timeline and want to close legal before the end of the month.

Best,
Tom
Tom Bennett
Head of Legal, AstraHealth

Attachment: Astra_DPA_2028-06-10_redline.pdf (PDF, 78KB)

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Tom Bennett <tom.bennett@astrahealth.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-06-11T11:04:00Z
Subject: Re: DPA redline — handback window and TTL carve-outs

Tom — thanks for the clear summary and the redline. I reviewed with Marcus (platform) and Jordan (product). High-level thoughts and a proposed compromise below. I'll follow up with a marked counter-redline by end of day tomorrow.

Handback / return window
- Your ask: 30-day handback to request final snapshot and transfer of onshore copies.
- Constraint: Our standard operational window to stage, validate, and securely transmit a final snapshot, plus coordinate KMS/transfer steps for BYOK, averages 45 days for EU onshore exports given current schedules and personnel.
- Proposed compromise language: 45-day handback period by default; customer may request an expedited state transfer within 15 days for an additional one-time operational fee and a documented runbook. For termination scenarios caused by Redwood material breach, the expedited fee is waived.

Tiered TTL carve-outs
- We can accept explicit tiering (logs / backups / ephemeral cache) but need precise definitions and maximums to operationalize.
- Proposal: logs = 180 days (compliant with incident investigation needs), ephemeral inference cache = 30 days (best-effort auto-erase, no guaranteed forensic persistence), backups (snapshots) = 90 days (with a retention carve-out allowing an additional 30 days for legal hold with notice).
- Onshore replication constraint: we can contractually commit to primary snapshot replication staying in EU-operated regions for EU-resident data. However, immutable backup copies used for long-term archive may reside in a geo-fallback region for DR; we propose a guarded exception where cross-border replication is permitted only if: (a) customer provides written consent at signing or later, or (b) a documented emergency DR invocation occurs and the replication is limited, logged, and certified within 7 days.

Certificates of erasure
- We can provide a deletion attestation for primary copies within 21 days. For backups, we can provide an attestation within 90 days after the deletion window elapses, noting that third-party archive providers may extend irrecoverability timing.

Next steps
- I'll circulate a clean Redwood counter-redline with the above language and a short glossary defining "ephemeral cache", "snapshot/backup", and "onshore copy".
- Marcus: can you confirm the operational feasibility of expedited transfers and approximate surcharge?

Thanks — aiming to get a binding draft back to you by COB tomorrow.

— Hannah
Hannah Schmitt
Head of Trust & Compliance, Redwood Inference
redwood.com

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-06-13T08:39:00Z
Subject: Re: DPA redline — handback window and TTL carve-outs

Hannah / Jordan — quick ops note on feasibility and cost for the proposed options:

- 45-day handback baseline: operationally fine. Standard runbook includes snapshot export, integrity checks, and secure transfer via customer-provided SFTP or presigned object URL. Average engineering effort: 12-18 hours spread over 2-3 engineers; typical calendar time 4-6 weeks to schedule.

- Expedited 15-day transfer: feasible but high-touch. We estimate a one-time surcharge of $6,500 to cover priority scheduling, manual validation, and extra ticket handling. If the customer provides full automation access (e.g., direct S3 bucket with transfer role and completed BYOK key handover), surcharge can be reduced to $2,500.

- 90-day backup attestation: we can generate deletion proofs for backups, but note there are edge-cases with third-party long-term archival (if customer elects archival to a partner) that extend irrecoverability. Our attestation will explicitly list those exceptions.

- Cross-border replication clause: to enforce this we need the contract to include a model mapping and the allowed target regions. We'll provide a template appendix that lists Redwood-controlled EU regions and the emergency DR process that triggers the guarded exception.

I'll add exact wording and the template appendix into the counter-redline Hannah is preparing.

- Marcus
Marcus Lin
VP, Platform Engineering | Redwood Inference

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Tom Bennett <tom.bennett@astrahealth.com>
Cc: legal@astrahealth.com, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-06-15T16:23:00Z
Subject: Re: DPA redline — handback window and TTL carve-outs (Redwood counter-proposal)

Tom — attaching Redwood's counter-redline and a short appendix covering definitions and the emergency DR exception. Summary of key points:

1) Handback window: 45 days standard; 15-day expedited option available with surcharge (waived in case of Redwood material breach). Implementation runbook is attached as Appendix A.

2) Tiered TTLs: logs = 180 days; ephemeral inference cache = 30 days; backups/snapshots = 90 days default, plus a 30-day legal-hold extension upon written notice.

3) Onshore replication: contractually restricts primary snapshot replication for EU-resident data to EU-operated regions. Cross-border replication for backups only under (a) customer written consent, or (b) documented emergency DR invocation; any such replication must be logged and certified within 7 days and reported to customer compliance point of contact.

4) Certificates of erasure: attestation for primary deletion within 21 days; backup attestation within 90 days with explicit listing of any third-party archival exceptions.

Please see the attached PDF for the exact redline and Appendix B (region mapping + emergency DR steps). If AstraHealth is agreeable to this compromise, we'd request a sign-off or a short call to finalize the wording. We can also provide the expedited transfer playbook and cost estimate if you want to enable the faster handback option.

Regards,
Hannah Schmitt
Head of Trust & Compliance, Redwood Inference
redwood.com

Attachments: Redwood_counter_redline_2028-06-15.pdf (PDF, 42KB), Appendix_A_runbook.docx (DOCX, 18KB)
